A Hong Kong EJC binds only Alpha and Beta. Alpha's loss was caused jointly by Beta and by two Singapore companies, C and D, which signed nothing. Alpha sues all three in Singapore. Beta seeks a stay.

If Beta's part goes to Hong Kong while C and D are sued here, the same facts are tried twice, with a risk of inconsistent findings and a race to judgment. If Alpha could not have foreseen C and D's involvement when it agreed to the clause, that fragmentation may be strong cause (Vinmar, citing Donohue).

But if the related foreign proceedings simply involve different parties, causes or remedies, that is not enough (Shanghai Turbo). And in a CCAA case, the same argument fails s 12(1)(c) outright (6DM).

✍ EXAM-READY SENTENCES
Strong cause, Singapore NEJC

Delta's application to set aside service objects to Singapore in breach of cl 18, so per Shanghai Turbo it must show strong cause (Vinmar). Its reliance on witnesses and documents in China and on related Chinese proceedings fails: those factors were foreseeable when it agreed to cl 18, and the Chinese proceedings involve different parties and remedies. Delta does not allege abuse or denial of justice, so it is held to its bargain.

6J4.4 The SICC factor

🧩 Practise J4.4 on hypotheticals →
▤ On your pre-write: J4.4 THE SICC FACTOR IN THE GENERAL DIVISION'S SPILIADA ANALYSIS (word for word)
J4.4 THE SICC FACTOR IN THE GENERAL DIVISION'S SPILIADA ANALYSIS (insert at J4.1.2 / J4.2)
  • Relevant (+) Presently, [claimant] resists [a stay / shows forum conveniens] by pointing to possible transfer to the SICC. Per Rappo, the court must not "shut its eyes" to [foreign law on submissions (s 18L) / international judges].
  • Internal Allocation Per Rappo (citing Yeo) and C&Y, transferring [the action] to the SICC is a later question of internal allocation (J5.4), and there must be no "unprincipled jurisdictional grab" for [the dispute].
  • Burden on Claimant (−) Per Rappo, the SICC is not "a free pass": [claimant] must name [the particular SICC feature] and show [the dispute] suits it, with the transfer requirements prima facie met; absent a prima facie international and commercial case, no weight.
  • Never Decisive (−) Per IM Skaugen, the judge erred in letting [the SICC factor] tip [a German-law, German-tort fraud claim] to Singapore; alone it cannot displace [State B], which "would virtually always" be the forum.
  • At Most a Discount (±) Per IM Skaugen, it discounts the weight of [law B], depending on similarity to Singapore law and complexity. Presently [law B] is [a similar common law system / civil law with complex issues], so the discount is [significant / slight].

In IM Skaugen, the judge erred in letting the SICC factor tip a German-law, German-tort fraud claim to Singapore: alone it cannot displace the foreign forum. How big the discount is depends on how similar the foreign law is to Singapore law and how complex the issues are.

★ IN PLAIN ENGLISH

Normally, "this dispute is governed by German law" pulls towards Germany, because German judges know German law and a Singapore court would need experts to prove it. The SICC can soften that pull: foreign law can be argued on submissions there (s 18L), and it has international judges. So the SICC factor works like a discount coupon on the foreign-law factor. It makes that factor lighter. It never adds a new weight of its own on Singapore's side of the scales.

7J4.5 Overlays: parallel proceedings

🧩 Practise J4.5 on hypotheticals →
▤ On your pre-write: J4.5 OVERLAYS: LIS ALIBI PENDENS, LIMITED STAY AND FORUM ELECTION (word for word)
J4.5 OVERLAYS: LIS ALIBI PENDENS, LIMITED STAY AND FORUM ELECTION
  • Three Routes Where [the dispute] is also pending in [X], [defendant] may rely on it at stage 1 (J4.1.2), seek a limited stay, or make a common claimant elect; it is no bar here, unlike the EU first-seised rule.
  • Limited Stay Per Rappo and 6DM, the court may stay [the Singapore action / part of it] pending [X's jurisdiction ruling / the related proceedings], managing [fragmentation risk] at an early stage.
  • Forum Election: Common Claimant Per Koh Kay Yew and Virsagi, where [claimant] sues [defendant] here and in [X] on [the same issues], it must elect unless it justifies the multiplicity, to "prevent the inherent abuse" of different judicial systems.
  • Case Management Only Per Rappo, election never fixes the trial forum: if [claimant] elects Singapore, [defendant] may still seek an FNC stay; if it elects [X], the action here is stayed and [defendant] may seek an ASI (Koh Kay Yew; J6).
    • Exception: unless [defendant] accepts [claimant]'s choice or made [a representation] that [claimant] relied on (Rappo).
  • FNC First Per Rappo, where [defendant] runs both, FNC is decided first, and election follows only if [X] is not clearly more appropriate, saving [resources] and following logic (C&Y).
  • Different Parties or Issues Election does not apply to [related proceedings] with different parties or issues, or where [defendant] sues in [X] (reversed parties); these go to FNC (J4.1.2) or an ASI (J6).
  • Limited stay. The court may stay the Singapore action, or part of it, pending the foreign jurisdiction ruling or related proceedings (Rappo; 6DM).
  • Election never fixes the trial forum. If the claimant elects Singapore, the defendant may still seek an FNC stay; if it elects the foreign forum, the action here is stayed (Rappo), unless the defendant accepted the choice or made a representation the claimant relied on.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Suing in two places at once

Alpha sues Beta in both Singapore and Kuala Lumpur over the same unpaid invoices.

  1. FNC first. Beta asks for a stay. If Malaysia is clearly more appropriate, the Singapore action is stayed under Spiliada and the election question never arises (Rappo).
  2. Then election. If Malaysia is not clearly more appropriate, Alpha is the claimant in both places, so it must elect one, unless it can justify running both (Koh Kay Yew; Virsagi).
  3. Different picture: if instead Beta had started the KL case, there is no election. The KL case is a stage 1 factor, or a reason for a limited stay, or a target for an ASI (J6).

8Put it together: two worked stays

✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Hypo 1: no clause

Alpha (Singapore) sues Beta, an Indonesian company registered in Singapore and served at its Singapore registered office (s 376 CA), for fraudulent misrepresentations made in Jakarta and relied on there. Indonesian law governs. Beta seeks a stay.

  1. Test (J4.0.2): no clause, served in, so Spiliada with stage 1 on Beta.
  2. Available: Indonesian courts have jurisdiction over Beta.
  3. Stage 1 (J4.1.2): the tort was committed in Indonesia (prima facie the natural forum, JIO), Indonesian law governs and witnesses are there. Indonesia is clearly more appropriate.
  4. Stage 2 (J4.1.3): Alpha says trial in Jakarta takes years and damages are lower. Neither suffices without cogent evidence of egregious delay (Grains and Industrial). Stay granted.
✎ WORKED EXAMPLE
Hypo 2: a Singapore EJC

Same facts, but the contract has "the courts of Singapore shall have exclusive jurisdiction". Beta seeks a stay.

  1. Test: Beta objects to the chosen forum, so strong cause on Beta (J4.3).
  2. Eleftheria (flipped): witnesses and Indonesian law were foreseeable. Beta alleges no abuse by Alpha and no concrete prejudice in defending here.
  3. Result: Beta is held to its bargain. No stay. (And if the CCAA applied, s 11 would require Singapore to hear the case anyway: J1.3.)
